question: According to Article 343 (1) of the Constitution of India, Hindi written in the Hindi script shall be the official language of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Devanagari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Devanagari is an alphasyllabary used in India and Nepal for languages such as Hindi, Marathi, Nepali, and Sanskrit.
 
• The script consists of 14 vowels and 33 consonants and is written from left to right.
 
• Devanagari script is highly phonetic, meaning that each character represents a specific sound.
 
• It is one of the most widely used and adopted writing systems in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 343 (1) of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• Article 343(1) states that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
 
• The form of numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union shall be the international form of Indian numerals.
 
• This article was adopted to promote a uniform language for the administration across the country.
 
 
 
• **Kharosthi Script**
 
 
• Kharosthi is an ancient script used in Gandhara, an ancient region in present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• It was used to write the Gandhari language and was in use from the 4th century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script**
 
 
• Brahmi is one of the oldest writing systems in South Asia, dating back to the 3rd century BCE.
 
• It is considered the mother of many modern Indian scripts, including Devanagari.
 
 
 
• **Indus Script**
 
 
• The Indus script is a writing system developed by the Indus Valley Civilization during the Bronze Age.
 
• It remains undeciphered and is one of the oldest known scripts in the world.
